clue.text: Response to warne's spinners

indicators.note: spinners are things that turn round, so the letters of the cricketer's name are spun into a new order

parts.note: the name Warne with its S, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reply to the deliveries of Shane Warne, the Australian spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Shane Warne was a famous Australian leg-spin bowler in cricket, so 'spinners' looks like his deliveries; it is the anagram signal working on the six letters of WARNE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply or retort is a response to a question.

clue.text: Aeroplane company owns special propeller

indicators.note: something that owns another holds it, so the letter goes inside the company of fliers

parts.note: the people who work an aircraft are its aircrew

explanation.surface: An aircraft firm possesses a particular propeller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aeroplane company' reads as an airline business, but it is the crew of a plane; 'owns' puts S inside AIRCREW.
explanation.definitionFit: An airscrew is the rotating blade assembly that drives an aircraft, i.e. its propeller.

clue.text: Prominently display modern spelling's origin

indicators.note: the origin is the starting point, so the abbreviation for spelling comes at the front

parts.note: sp. is the dictionary abbreviation for spelling
latter can mean recent or modern, as in latter-day

explanation.surface: Showing off where today's spelling comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin' places SP at the start, ahead of LATTER; the surface suggests etymology but no word history is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter a story across the front page is to splash it, displaying it conspicuously.

clue.text: From the sound of it deserve the bird

indicators.note: this phrase says we want a word that is pronounced like the synonym rather than spelt like it

parts.note: to deserve something is to earn it

explanation.surface: Apparently the bird has earned what it gets.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Bookkeeper, perhaps, and sailor feign an eye problem

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant, of which a bookkeeper is a loose example
tar is an old word for a sailor
to feign is to act or pretend

explanation.surface: An accountant and a seaman pretend to have trouble with their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: CA (chartered accountant) is signalled with 'perhaps' because a bookkeeper is only roughly an accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a clouding of the lens that dims sight, a common ailment of vision.

clue.text: Heather, pa and Tim performed on open-air stage

indicators.note: performed suggests acting, but here it says the three names are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Three amateur actors put on a show at an outdoor theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' rearranges HEATHER, PA and TIM; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is an unroofed arena with tiers of seats round a central performing space.

clue.text: Voice lallation regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of lallation

explanation.surface: Speech made of baby babble, done routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: Lallation is babbling or the mispronunciation of R as L; 'regularly' picks its even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singing part pitched below soprano, a type of singing range.

clue.text: First sign of sun being eclipsed comes into view

indicators.note: something eclipsed is hidden behind something else, so the letter for the sun is enclosed by the star sign

parts.note: Aries is the first sign of the zodiac
S is the abbreviation for sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: The sun first appears after an eclipse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First sign' looks like an early hint, but it is ARIES, which starts the zodiac; 'being eclipsed' puts S inside it, and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to appear or emerge, as a problem or a sun does.

clue.text: A number departed in the first twin-hulled yacht

indicators.note: in places the word for departed inside the pair of initial letters
the first letters of the words twin-hulled and yacht are taken

parts.note: departed means went

explanation.surface: Someone sailed away aboard the first catamaran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first' takes T and Y from 'twin-hulled yacht'; 'in' puts WENT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is the whole number after nineteen, a score.

clue.text: Relax about a period of abstinence

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Ease off concerning a time of self-denial.
explanation.walkthrough: LENT is the Christian season of fasting before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften or ease up on a harsh position, to let up.

clue.text: Flame-thrower?

parts.note: read literally, something that throws out fire, such as a fiery-tempered person or a gun firing tracer, rather than the military weapon

explanation.definitionFit: A spitfire is a hot-tempered person who spits out anger, and also the famous fighter plane whose guns blazed.

clue.text: Boxer, a surging mass of power, could be 67kg

parts.note: a welter is a confused, tossing mass, as of waves
weight means power or influence, as in carrying weight

explanation.surface: A fighter described as a heaving bulk of strength, possibly weighing 67kg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be 67kg' adds that the class tops out at about 67 kilograms (147 pounds).
explanation.definitionFit: A welterweight is a fighter in the class between lightweight and middleweight.

clue.text: Astute copper of note

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A clever policeman of some renown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal; 'note' is TE from do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in an older sense means clever or shrewd.

clue.text: Start to ask for charity at home

parts.note: to beg is to ask for alms
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Commence asking for donations from one's own house.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin is to commence.

clue.text: After gymnastics, saint became a troublemaker

indicators.note: after says the abbreviation for saint follows the one for gymnastics

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gymnastics

explanation.surface: A holy person turned nuisance after a gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is a nuisance, someone who causes bother.

clue.text: Easily annoyed but, technologically, no reasonable lecturer would be excluded

indicators.note: says the following pieces are taken out of the long word technologically

parts.note: reasonable means logical

explanation.surface: Irritable, but no sensible teacher would be shut out by technology.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing NO, LOGICAL and L, which run together in the middle of TECHNOLOGICALLY, leaves TECH and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Techy is a variant spelling of tetchy, meaning irritable or touchy.

clue.text: Soundly rebuke alternative teacher

parts.note: tut is the clicking noise made to scold someone
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Give a vocal telling-off to a stand-in teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' or like a hint about pronunciation; it says the rebuke is a noise, TUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private instructor who gives lessons.

clue.text: Some words from Matthew (ch 20, v6-9) given at the very last moment

definitions.meaning: in the parable of the vineyard labourers, the last workers are hired late in the day yet paid a full wage
an idiom for just before it is too late

explanation.surface: A biblical citation supplied just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: In Matthew 20 the master hires idle men at about five in the afternoon, the phrase that gave the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from the late-hired workers of the gospel parable and now means a final, almost too late, point in time.

clue.text: Recycle bin, for instance, is created for waste disposal

indicators.note: disposal hints at getting rid of rubbish, but it says the letters of for waste are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recycling bin exists to get rid of refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycle bin' is a computer's deleted-files folder, not a kerbside container; 'disposal' rearranges FOR WASTE, and 'is created' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Recycle Bin is a program feature on a computer, an example of code run by a machine.

clue.text: Get similar parts from stamp company

parts.note: a stamp or type is a block that prints a character
the cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Obtain matching components from a printing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' are acting roles and 'company' is the theatre troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast is always given the same sort of role.

clue.text: Sounds like the science of agriculture could involve opium, for example

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken like a phrase meaning farm studies, not spelt like it

parts.note: farm ecology, said quickly, is the study of farming systems

explanation.surface: Agricultural science might include growing poppies for opium.
explanation.walkthrough: FARM ECOLOGY is a made-up phrase whose spoken form resembles the answer; the definition is cryptic, opium being one drug the field studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharmacology is the study of drugs and their effects, which could take in a narcotic such as the poppy's resin.

clue.text: As hurricane hit marina — pilot needed

indicators.note: a storm striking the harbour throws everything about, so the letters of marina are jumbled

explanation.surface: A storm struck the harbour and a flier was required.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hurricane was also a British wartime fighter plane, which fits the pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman is a flier, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Instrument not involved with making wine

indicators.note: not says the letters for involved are left out of the woodwind instrument

parts.note: the clarinet is a woodwind instrument
in means involved, as in being in on a plan

explanation.surface: A musical instrument plays no part in winemaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes IN out of CLARINET; 'with making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, a red vintage.

clue.text: Walk slowly but I would still be in front of the French

indicators.note: in front of places the contraction ahead of the French article

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I would
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Stroll leisurely, yet I'd still lead the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' and 'still be' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle along is to move lazily or saunter.

clue.text: Possessively, I go astray in causing laughter

indicators.note: in places the word for straying inside the possessive pronoun

parts.note: the possessive form of I is my
to err is to go wrong or stray

explanation.surface: I wander off in a way that amuses people.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry means jolly and full of fun, provoking mirth.

clue.text: Swine location on parts of both unst and Skye

indicators.note: parts of says only a fragment of the Shetland island's name is used, its last two letters
both extends the same taking of a fragment to the second island, Skye, again its final pair

explanation.surface: A pigsty sited on two Scottish islands, Unst and Skye.
explanation.walkthrough: Unst is the northernmost Shetland island and Skye an island of the Inner Hebrides; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stye is a variant spelling of sty, a pen where pigs are kept.

clue.text: Meat dish from kinknockie village butchers

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, Kinknockie village

explanation.surface: A chicken dish bought at a Scottish village's butcher's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinknockie is a small village in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken Kiev is a breaded chicken fillet stuffed with garlic butter, often called a Kiev.

clue.text: Irish father, first from a set of two

indicators.note: first says the word for father comes before the abbreviation for Irish

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An Irish dad is the first of a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of a kind taken together, a couple.

clue.text: Awfully grim area for a union meeting

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of grim area are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dreary place for a trade union gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union meeting' suggests a trade union assembly; 'union' is the definition and 'for a' and 'meeting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is the joining of two people as spouses, a wedlock.

clue.text: This land is able to support a lawyer

parts.note: can means is able to
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A country that can afford to keep an attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is an American district attorney; 'to support' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a country in North America.

clue.text: Ingenious about odds of 4:1 on one's nationality at birth

indicators.note: about says the smart word goes round the Roman figures

parts.note: natty can mean clever or deft
the betting odds written in Roman numerals give IV and I

explanation.surface: A clever bookmaker's odds based on where someone was born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' looks like betting, but 4 and 1 become Roman IV and I; 'on one's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nativity means birth, and in older use the place or land of one's birth.

clue.text: Bring, a queen and all others, to a standstill

parts.note: R stands for regina, Latin for queen
the rest means all the others

explanation.surface: Halt a queen and everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The full definition 'Bring ... to a standstill' wraps round the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest is to stop or halt something, bringing it to a stop.
